World building, one region at a time

From WoW terrain
to your Blender world.

Build the toolkit, bring a landscape into Blender, and prepare its geometry for navigation. A practical guide for this customized wow.export checkout.

Windows x64Blender 5.0+Illustrated workflowSource & release instructions
01 /Choose your starting point

Using it or building it?

For artists & end users

Use the release download

Get the Windows installer ZIP or portable ZIP from GitHub Releases. You need Blender 5.0+ to use the addon. Developer tools are only needed if you build from source.

Go to installation →
For developers

Build your own version

Use Visual Studio C++ tools, CMake, Bun, Node.js, and Python. The CMake project builds the native geometry helper and exposes the application build.

Go to build instructions →
WoW data→wow.export→ADT exported as OBJ→Blender→Navigation geometry
An ADT goes through wow.export first.Blender’s addon imports the exported adt_*.obj and its companion files. Select the OBJ in Blender, rather than the original raw .adt.
02 /Get ready

Install once. Keep the files together.

  1. Download the Windows release

    Choose wow-export-win-x64-0.2.21.zip for the installer, or portable-wow-export-win-x64-0.2.21.zip for a portable copy. Extract the whole ZIP.

  2. Launch wow.export

    For the installer, run installer.exe beside data.pak and data.pak.json. It installs under %LOCALAPPDATA%\wow.export. For the portable package, run wow.export.exe in the extracted folder. Keep its DLLs and resources beside it.

  3. Install the Blender addon

    Start Blender once so its configuration folder exists. In wow.export’s menu, choose Install Blender Add-on → Install Automatically. Restart Blender, then enable Import WoW OBJ files with doodads under Edit → Preferences → Add-ons.

Prefer a manual Blender install?

Download io_scene_wowobj.zip from the release, or use the ZIP inside the app’s addon directory. In Blender 5.2, open Edit → Preferences → Add-ons, open the menu at the upper right, and select Install from Disk…. Choose the ZIP, enable the addon, and restart Blender. Menu placement can vary between Blender versions.

What success looks likeIn the 3D Viewport, press N and open the wow.export tab. You should see Import WoW OBJ, Import Last Export, Import Navigation Region, and Export Navigation Geometry—the controls visible in the screenshot above.
03 /Start small

Your first terrain tile.

  1. Export one tile from wow.export

    Choose your installed WoW client or an available online build, open the map tools, select a map, and export one terrain tile as OBJ. Include placed models and liquids if you want them in the scene. Enable texture export if you want a textured result.

  2. Preserve the export folder structure

    Keep adt_37_37.obj, its MTL, any placement CSV, liquid JSON, textures, and referenced model directories in their original relative locations. Moving only the OBJ loses the references needed for a complete scene.

  3. Import the exported OBJ

    In Blender, open the wow.export sidebar and choose Import WoW OBJ. Select the terrain OBJ. For a visual scene, leave model and texture options enabled. For geometry and pathing work, enable Navigation Geometry Only.

  4. Let the import reach 100%

    The status bar reports the import stage and percentage. Wait for completion before checking the result. The final linking stage can take time; geometry may appear near the end. Press Esc to cancel and remove the partial import.

  5. Inspect and save the scene

    Use Home to frame the scene, or select an object and press Numpad . to frame it. Orbit with the middle mouse button. Save a .blend before continuing.

Rendering

Want the textures?

Export textures and enable Import Textures. Switch the viewport to Material Preview. Solid shading displays gray geometry even when materials are present.

Pathing & large regions

Keep geometry lightweight

Navigation Geometry Only skips textures, materials, UVs, and animation data while retaining placed geometry and liquids. The Windows native parser accelerates this mode; Python is the fallback.

04 /Prepare a walkable world

Work in regions.

For navigation work, use Import Navigation Region and choose a center adt_*.obj. It selects nearby exported tiles and uses geometry-only import.

Neighbor RadiusMaximum regionUse it for
01 tileA first check or a small local fix
13 × 3 tilesA useful starting region; the default
25 × 5 tilesA larger area when memory allows

Only tiles actually present in the export directory are imported. Begin with radius 0, then increase it after confirming the result.

  1. Select the terrain roots

    Select the imported terrain roots so their placed objects and liquid children are included. Keep only the region you intend to export selected.

  2. Export Navigation Geometry

    Choose the sidebar control shown in the screenshot. Set the WoW Map ID to the client’s instance map ID—for example, 1 for Kalimdor. This is different from the UI map ID. Save the OBJ; the exporter also writes a matching .gset project.

  3. Open and bake in WoW Navigation Studio

    WoW Navigation Studio is a separate application from the sibling recastnavigation project. Open the .gset through OBJ / GSET → Open WoW world. Use Tile Mesh → Build. Review doors, corners, and liquids, save your edits, rebuild, then use Export baked mesh to write a .wnav and update world.wnavindex.

Start with one region before all of Kalimdor.Whole-continent textured imports can exceed available memory. Use geometry-only regions for navigation. Portal and custom-path links require deliberate setup in Navigation Studio; adding a link does not itself execute a teleport.
05 /Developer instructions

Build from source.

These commands target this customized Windows checkout. Run them from the repository root in a Visual Studio x64 developer terminal.

ToolRequirement / tested setup
Visual StudioDesktop development with C++; Windows SDK; CMake and Ninja. Tested with Visual Studio 2026 and MSVC v145.
CMake3.21 or newer; bundled with the Visual Studio CMake tools.
Bun1.2+ required; Release build tested with 1.3.5.
Node.js + npmNode 24.9.0+; npm is used to install node-gyp.
Python + node-gypPython 3 on PATH. Tested with Python 3.13 and node-gyp 13.1.0.
Get the source & dependencies
git clone https://github.com/xhonorbuddy/wow.export.git
cd wow.export
npm install -g node-gyp
bun install --frozen-lockfile

The repository is private at the time this guide was written. Cloning requires a GitHub account with access. Bun and the application build download dependencies and runtime files, so the first build needs internet access.

Build Windows Release
cmake --preset x64-release
cmake --build --preset app-release

app-release builds the native geometry helper first, copies its DLL beside the addon, and runs the Bun/NW.js application pipeline. The customized CMake target uses --local, which marks this build as local so the upstream updater does not replace it.

Just the Blender helper

A faster native build

Release helper
cmake --preset x64-release
cmake --build --preset native-release

Close Blender if it has loaded the DLL before replacing it.

Inside Visual Studio

Open the folder

Use File → Open → Folder. Select x64-release and build wow_export_app. A default build compiles the native helper only. If the folder was opened before CMake was enabled, reopen it.

Debug equivalents: x64-debug, native-debug, and app-debug.

This machine has presets ending in “-local”

Its CMakeUserPresets.json supplies Windows SDK paths that were missing from the automated terminal’s environment. Use x64-release-local and app-release-local on this machine if needed. That file is intentionally excluded from Git; other machines should use the normal presets with their own installed toolchain. Set BUN_EXECUTABLE to the full Bun path if CMake cannot find it.

Build outputPurpose
bin/win-x64/wow.export.exeThe application, with runtime files in the same folder
bin/win-x64-installer/installer.exe, data.pak, and data.pak.json
addons/blender/io_scene_wowobj.zipFreshly generated Blender install ZIP
out/build/CMake build directories; excluded from Git
06 /Give people a download

Share a release, not just the repository.

A GitHub repository is the source. A GitHub Release is where you attach the ready-to-run downloads and send your users.

Package the completed Windows build
bun publish.js win-x64

Despite its name, this command creates local archives under publish/win-x64/. It does not upload them to GitHub.

Upload this fileWho needs it?
wow-export-win-x64-0.2.21.zip
Recommended download		Windows users who want the installer. Contains the EXE and its two data files.
portable-wow-export-win-x64-0.2.21.zipUsers who prefer to extract the full app and run it directly.
io_scene_wowobj.zipUsers who only need to install or update the Blender addon.
wow-export-guide.htmlThis illustrated offline guide, with the screenshot embedded.
SHA256SUMS.txtOptional checksums to help users verify the downloaded files.
update / update.jsonUpdater payloads. Ordinary users should download the installer or portable ZIP instead.

  1. Test the exact files you will upload

    Extract the installer ZIP into a new folder, run the installer, open the app, install the bundled addon, and import one real ADT export in Blender. Verify the progress finishes and placed models and liquids appear as expected.

  2. Create a draft GitHub Release

    Open xhonorbuddy/wow.export → Releases and choose Draft a new release. Choose a unique version tag and title, for example v0.2.21-custom.1. Attach the installer ZIP, optionally the portable ZIP, the addon ZIP, and this guide.

  3. Publish and share the download link

    After testing, publish the release. Share the release page or its installer asset link. The Source code (zip) link generated by GitHub is source code, not an installer.

Private repository = restricted download.The repository is currently private. Only people with access can open its releases. For public downloads, either make an intentional decision to publish the repository or use a separate public distribution repository and upload the built assets there.
Links to share after a release is published

https://github.com/xhonorbuddy/wow.export/releases/download/v0.2.21-custom.1/wow-export-win-x64-0.2.21.zip

The specific tag URL above is an example, not a release created by this guide. A “latest” link exists only after an eligible release has been published.

About the existing GitHub Actions release workflow

The inherited tag workflow builds several platforms and calls an upstream update webhook using WOW_EXPORT_V2_UPDATE_KEY. It also needs permission to upload release assets. Adapt that workflow for this fork before relying on automated tag releases; manual packaging and upload are the documented path here. The native Blender helper is built by the CMake workflow described above.

Before you press Publish

07 /Find the next step

When something looks wrong.

Blender has no wow.export sidebar

Enable Import WoW OBJ files with doodads in Preferences, restart Blender, then press N over the 3D Viewport. If the addon cannot enable, make sure you installed the whole ZIP and are running Blender 5.0+.

The imported scene is gray

Gray is expected in Solid shading and in Navigation Geometry Only mode. For a textured scene, export textures, import with Import Textures enabled, and use Material Preview.

The terrain appears but objects or liquids are missing

Keep the original export directory structure. Check that the placement CSV and liquid JSON were exported, and that the referenced model files exist. A completion warning can report missing model files. If model export or liquid import was disabled, those elements will not appear.

Import is slow, or Blender uses too much memory

Start with one tile. Use Navigation Geometry Only for pathing, or Import Navigation Region with radius 0 or 1. A continent’s textures can exhaust RAM even when its geometry fits. Progress describes completed stages; it is not a time estimate.

Visual Studio still shows “No Configurations”

Reopen the repository folder. Verify .vs/CMakeWorkspaceSettings.json contains "enableCMake": true. Install CMake tools and a Windows SDK through the Visual Studio Installer. From an x64 developer terminal, check cmake --list-presets.

CMake cannot find Bun, rc.exe, or kernel32.lib

For Bun, install it on PATH and reconfigure, or pass -DBUN_EXECUTABLE=C:/path/to/bun.exe when configuring. For Windows SDK errors, use an x64 developer terminal with the complete SDK installed. A local user preset may be needed on a machine whose developer environment omits SDK paths.

The native DLL cannot be replaced

Close Blender instances that have loaded native_geometry.dll, then rebuild. Windows locks a DLL while a running process uses it.

The installer says data.pak is missing

Extract the entire installer ZIP. Run installer.exe from the folder containing data.pak and data.pak.json. Downloading or moving only the EXE is insufficient.

The release app exits before a window opens

Keep the complete runtime folder together. Check for a debug.log beside the EXE, and retain its exact error. An automated launch during this validation failed inside Chromium sandbox initialization; normal desktop startup still needs your test. This guide does not recommend disabling Chromium’s sandbox.
